transcript.text:
(You are behind the counter, dusting a bolt of imported silk with a feather duster. The door chimes as a tall, lanky man in a rumpled suit enters, his stovepipe hat nearly grazing the doorframe.)

"Welcome to 'The Fine Stitch'! You've caught us at a quiet moment, sir. Master Finch is away on a rather extensive business trip, won't be back for several weeks, I'm afraid. But I'd be happy to assist with anything you might need in the meantime. New orders, perhaps? Or a fitting for something we've already crafted?"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Good afternoon. I've come about a custom-made suit. It was ordered some time ago, but there seems to have been a misunderstanding regarding the materials used. I'd like to speak with the owner of this establishment."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Ah, a custom order! I see. As I mentioned, Master Finch is away – he left quite suddenly on a purchasing trip to New York, and he won't be back for a good long while, certainly not before the end of the month. So I'm afraid speaking with him directly isn't an option at present.

Now, regarding materials... all custom orders are final upon pickup, sir. The receipt Mr. Lincoln signed states clearly that no alterations or refunds are given once the garment leaves the shop. Master Finch is very particular about that clause, ensures every customer understands it before they sign. Are you Mr. Lincoln, by chance?"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Yes, I am indeed Mr. Abraham Lincoln. I believe there's been a mistake with my order. The suit is of inferior quality to what was agreed upon, and the stitching is quite subpar. I'd like to discuss this matter and have the suit altered or receive a refund."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Mr. Lincoln! A pleasure to finally meet you, though I wish it were under happier circumstances. My name is Thomas, Master Finch's assistant.

I do understand your concern, sir, but the policy is quite firm, as it was explained and signed for at the time of pickup. Once a custom garment leaves the shop, particularly after it's been worn, we simply cannot offer alterations or refunds. Master Finch is very particular about upholding the integrity of his agreements, and that clause protects against any misunderstandings or changes of mind once the work is complete and accepted. I assure you, every stitch and every yard of fabric used would have been precisely what was discussed and recorded in the order book."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "I understand the policy, Thomas, but this isn't just a matter of a change of mind. This suit is visibly flawed, and I believe the customer deserves satisfaction. I'm willing to work within the confines of the policy to find a solution that addresses the issue."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Mr. Lincoln, I truly do regret that you find yourself dissatisfied. However, the clause regarding 'no alterations or refunds' applies to all aspects once the garment has left the shop, including any claims of visible flaws that were not brought to our attention at the moment of pickup. Master Finch prides himself on the quality of his work, and it's understood that the garment is inspected and accepted as satisfactory when it is taken home. That is precisely why the receipt is signed.

I assure you, no expense was spared on the materials specified in your order, and our stitching is always held to the highest standard. Without Master Finch here to personally review the original order and your concerns, and with the strict policy in place for garments that have already left the premises... well, my hands are tied, sir. There isn't an avenue for alteration or refund once that contract has been fulfilled and accepted."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thomas, I appreciate your dedication to the policy and your understanding of Master Finch's meticulous standards. However, this suit was purchased with the intention of wearing it for a significant event, and I find myself unable to fulfill my commitment due to the flaws in the garment. I'm not looking for a refund or an alteration; I simply wish to address this matter in a manner that maintains the integrity of the transaction and demonstrates a commitment to customer satisfaction. Perhaps there is a way we can find a compromise that respects the policy while still upholding the dignity and purpose of the suit."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Mr. Lincoln, I do hear you, and I certainly understand the importance of a suit, especially for the kind of engagements I imagine you attend. It's truly regrettable that you feel the garment doesn't meet the dignity or purpose you intended.

However, the policy Master Finch has in place, which you signed for, is quite specific to the individual garment once it has left the shop. My authority as assistant is primarily to take new orders or manage fittings for *upcoming* projects. For a completed order, one that's been signed for and taken possession of... well, that transaction is considered closed on our end, as per the agreement.

To uphold the 'integrity of the transaction' as you say, we rely on the signed receipt as confirmation that the garment was accepted as satisfactory. With Master Finch away for weeks, and with that clear policy, I am truly at a loss for how to address your concerns regarding *this particular suit* while remaining within my authority. I simply cannot go against what was agreed upon and signed, especially in his absence."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you for your understanding, Thomas. I respect the policies in place, and I understand that altering or refunding the suit would require significant changes to the existing system. Instead, I'd like to offer a different solution. I'm willing to donate the suit to a charity or institution that supports individuals in need of proper attire for formal events. In doing so, I believe I can fulfill my commitment to attending these events while also providing a benefit to others who may not have such opportunities. Would you consider this alternative? It's a compromise that still honors the principles of the transaction while maintaining its intended purpose."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Mr. Lincoln, that's certainly... a very generous and thoughtful idea on your part, to consider donating the garment to a worthy cause. A most benevolent gesture, I'd say.

However, from the perspective of 'The Fine Stitch,' once the suit was picked up and the receipt signed, the transaction for that specific garment was considered complete and final. What you choose to do with the suit now, as its owner – whether you wear it, store it, or indeed, donate it – is entirely your prerogative

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you for your understanding, Thomas. I appreciate your adherence to the policy. Given the circumstances, I will accept that the transaction is considered complete upon pickup. I'll take responsibility for the suit and ensure it is used for a purpose that aligns with the spirit of the event I had intended to attend. Thank you for your assistance, and please convey my gratitude to Master Finch upon his return."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Very well, Mr. Lincoln. I appreciate your understanding of our policies, and your decision to make good use of the garment in a way that suits your intentions. It's a commendable approach, sir.

I will absolutely convey your message and your gratitude to Master Finch the moment he returns from his travels. I'm sure he will be pleased to hear of your thoughtfulness. Is there anything else I can assist you with today, perhaps a new order for future needs, or some accessories?"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "No, I believe that covers everything for now, Thomas. Thank you for your assistance, and I'll keep your words of gratitude in mind. Good day to you."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Good day to you too, Mr. Lincoln. Thank you for visiting 'The Fine Stitch.' Do take care now."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "You're welcome. Take care, and again, thank you for your understanding."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "My pleasure, Mr. Lincoln. Always happy to assist as best I can. Do call on us again should you have any need for Master Finch's services in the future."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "I shall keep that in mind. Thank you again, Thomas."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "You're most welcome, sir. Safe travels."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Safe travels, indeed. Thank you for your time."
